clue.text: (&17) Brenda's with Roger for life possibly

definitions.note: a phrase, standing for an indefinite prison term that may last a lifetime

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for the Queen, so Brenda's is the possessive of Her Majesty
to roger is British slang for having sex, so the word stands for sexual pleasure

explanation.surface: A gossip item: the Queen has taken up with someone called Roger, perhaps for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda. A prisoner held at Her Majesty's pleasure is detained with no fixed release date, which can mean for life.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention at the monarch's pleasure is an indeterminate sentence in British law, so it may well amount to imprisonment for life.

clue.text: Real beauty of a stink over bell-ringer

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a dinger is something that dings, as a bell does

explanation.surface: A smell hanging over a campanologist, which turns out to be a true beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: A humdinger is an informal word for something outstanding of its kind, a real beauty.

clue.text: Raises arses

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lifts or brings up, as a verb
second meaning: a plural noun, rear ends

explanation.walkthrough: Two words that read like a rude rhyme are two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to lift or bring up, and rears are also backsides, the vulgar noun's polite synonym.

clue.text: Disorderly Jeffrey has no hesitation getting into "I can" mode

indicators.note: the shortened surname goes inside the other letters
in a mode suggests a different arrangement, so the letters of I can are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist and Tory peer, a frequent Private Eye target
er, the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Lord Archer, jailed for perjury in 2001, losing his hesitancy and getting into a can-do mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Conservative peer, was much mocked in Private Eye. The rearranged letters split round the shortened name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means lawless and chaotic, so it is a synonym of disorderly.

clue.text: Peers' sort of sign

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... are one's peers, people of the same standing
second meaning: the arithmetic symbol of two parallel bars

explanation.walkthrough: Peers suggests the House of Lords, but it means people of equal rank; the sign is the one in sums.
explanation.definitionFit: One's equals are one's peers, and the equals sign is the mathematical symbol for equality.

clue.text: Going through the motions as a lover?

definitions.meaning: normally means doing something half-heartedly, but here the motions are literal movements
the question mark flags that the motions are those of sex

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for acting without enthusiasm is taken literally, as the repeated movements of lovemaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrusting is the pushing movement of sex, the literal motions a lover goes through.

clue.text: Short girl, very round, gets barrage of insults

parts.note: Sal is a short form of the name Sally
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A small, very plump young woman is subjected to a stream of abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, and by extension a sudden burst of criticism or insults.

clue.text: "Bang?" Lola scoffed, "hasn't got an earthly!"

indicators.note: a word sneered out is mangled, so the letters are rearranged
the remaining letters lack the two letters of an

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A woman named Lola mocks the idea of sex: he has not got an earthly chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hasn't got an earthly is British slang for having no chance at all; earthly then serves alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Global means relating to the whole Earth, so it can stand for earthly in the sense of worldwide.

clue.text: Description of content of smelly sock written down to ingratiate yourself

definitions.text: Description of content of smelly sock written down
definitions.meaning: a word is hidden backwards in the letters of smelly sock, so in a down light it reads upward; the answer describes that
to make yourself friendly with someone to win favour

explanation.walkthrough: Inside smellY SOCk sits YSOC, which is COSY read backwards; in a down light it is written going up, so it is COSY UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosy up to someone is to make friends with them for advantage, an idiom for currying favour.

clue.text: Thrash: one including wicked dance

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces takes the next word's letters inside them

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash someone
A, the indefinite article, is one
bad, the plain synonym

explanation.surface: A grumble that some wild, naughty dance amounts to a beating.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes Thrash look like a definition, but it is the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance that was a craze around 1990.

clue.text: Artist freaked out, astride Brook

indicators.note: something astride another sits with a part on each side of it, so these letters go round the next piece
freaked means thrown into disorder, so the letters of out are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: A painter has panicked and is standing straddling a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Freaked out reads as one phrase meaning panicked, but freaked is the anagram signal and out is its fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French painter famous for his Montmartre street scenes, so he is a well-known artist.

clue.text: Naff awards presenter's butt in shreds

indicators.note: the presenter's final letter goes inside the word for shreds

parts.note: bits, small torn pieces
the butt is the end of something, so the presenter's end is the word's final letter

explanation.surface: Some tacky awards show ends with its host's backside torn to ribbons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brits are the British music industry's annual awards; naff is British slang for tacky or uncool, a fair jibe from Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The BRIT Awards are Britain's pop music prizes, here dismissed with a slang word for tasteless.

clue.text: Mostly worried about nothing following business procedure to divert motions

indicators.note: the rest comes after the abbreviation for a business firm

parts.note: Co., short for company

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the letter for nothing
worried here means pulled about, so the letters of the clue's first word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Someone fretful about getting nowhere with business rules meant to sidetrack proposals at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mostly looks like it trims a word, but it is the anagram fodder itself. Motions means meeting proposals on the surface and bowel movements in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A colostomy is surgery that reroutes the colon through an opening in the abdomen, so waste leaves by a new route.

clue.text: English lass getting screwed outside — assistance needed by suitor?

indicators.note: the word for screwed wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: laid, crude slang for having had sex
gal, an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: An English girl being bedded, and a would-be wooer who needs a hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Suitor is not a wooer but someone bringing a lawsuit; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is state funding for people who cannot afford a lawyer, which a litigant may well need.

clue.text: Pissed Cyclops, on 'Wickets', makes a case of it

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk, as pissed is in Britain
the setter's pseudonym; the setter refers to themself as I
a wicket is a small gate, so wickets are gates

explanation.surface: The setter, drunk, riffs on wickets and ends up making a whole court case out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter's own pseudonym, and setters call themselves I. A wicket is a small door or gate, not only cricket stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take a matter to court, literally to make a legal case of it.

clue.text: Casual partner's tool getting erect …

parts.note: a pick is a digging tool
standing up, so the word is up

explanation.surface: A smutty line about a one-night stand's equipment rising to the occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next, but each has its own answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickup is someone met and taken home casually, a short-term sexual partner.

clue.text: Got out of bed with child

definitions.meaning: first meaning: woken by knocking, an old British usage
second meaning: made pregnant, in crude slang

explanation.walkthrough: In older British English to knock someone up is to wake them by knocking at their door; elsewhere it means to make pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both rousing a sleeper and, as slang, making a woman pregnant.

clue.text: (See 1 Across)
… is worth a great many tries to be refined

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many

indicators.note: to refine is to work something over and change it, so the letters of tries are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: it deserves plenty of attempts before it is polished.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to deserve it, so merits is the verb meaning is worth.

clue.text: Menacing type of clue, mixed with s and m

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: S and M suggest sadomasochism, but they are just two letters added to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is slang for a heavy or thug employed to intimidate, a menacing type.

clue.text: Penny has vulgar organ that gurgles in the bath

parts.note: lughole is coarse British slang for the ear

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny has a rude body part that makes noises in the tub.
explanation.walkthrough: Vulgar organ promises something ruder than an ear. P is the abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A plughole is the drain hole in a bath, which gurgles as the water runs out.

clue.text: Being provocative, going topless and giving relief

indicators.note: losing the top, in a down answer the first letter

parts.note: teasing, deliberately provoking

explanation.surface: A flirt who strips off her top and so offers some comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing pain is relieving it, so easing means giving relief.

clue.text: Performance with nothing to see, but he gets paid for doing it

definitions.text: he gets paid for doing it

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
O looks like zero
lo, an old exclamation meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A show where nothing is visible, yet the performer still gets his fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Doing it is a euphemism for sex, so the paid man is not a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to be a lover or companion, usually to an older woman.

clue.text: Fantastic shag, right in the city Hilton's paradise

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
LA, Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Paris Hilton's idea of heaven: a great romp in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilton suggests Paris Hilton, but it is James Hilton, whose novel Lost Horizon invented the hidden utopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the secluded Himalayan valley of perfect contentment in James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon.

clue.text: Muddled Labour's second seat lost

indicators.note: only the second letter of the party's name is used

parts.note: only its second letter is used

indicators.note: lost suggests something astray, so the letters of seat are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A confused Labour Party loses a second parliamentary seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed count (2,5) is wrong for a five-letter light; the phrase is two and three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being bewildered or confused, muddled.

clue.text: All right to interrupt workout with Bob's balls

OK

clue.text: Breathe heavily catching first sight of lacy gear

explanation.walkthrough: Gear looks like clothing to go with lacy, but it means machinery.

clue.text: Excessive piss-taker inhabiting awful hole in the country

indicators.note: the drunkard lives inside the rearranged letters

explanation.walkthrough: Piss-taker usually means a mocker; here it is literally someone who takes too much piss, meaning booze.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Making out what this sort of discussion has come to mean

definitions.meaning: having sex, the meaning the word has come to carry

definitions.text: what this sort of discussion has come to mean
definitions.meaning: points to a Private Eye catchphrase in which a kind of talks became a byword for sex

explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye reported a guest 'discussing Uganda' with a woman upstairs at a party, and 'Ugandan discussions' became its euphemism for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: In Private Eye's in-joke, Ugandan discussions are sexual encounters, so the adjective now signals sex.

clue.text: Bottom's experience of being head over heels

definitions.meaning: reads like Shakespeare's Bottom, but means what happens to your rear end
the somersault position, which puts the rear above the top

explanation.walkthrough: Arse over tip is British slang for head over heels; in a somersault your backside really does go over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase describes tumbling upside down, the literal sense of tumbling heels over head.
